entries.name: ToolOracle AgentGuard
entries.description: MCP guardrail server that vets agent tool-calls before execution: computes a 0-100 risk score, runs policy pre-flight (allow/deny/require_approval), checks/manages human approvals, verifies MCP tool manifests for prompt-injection, and reports guard metrics.

content.text: <stringified JSON result for the called tool>

usage.callShape: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST to https://tooloracle.io/guard/mcp/ with Content-Type: application/json (and Accept: application/json). Handshake once: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"masterkey","version":"1.0"}}}. Then invoke a tool: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":N,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}. The tool result JSON arrives stringified in result.content[0].text.
usage.outputShape: JSON-RPC envelope: result.content[0].text is a JSON string. For tool_risk_score: {tool_name, agent_id, risk_score, risk_level, recommendation, risk_factors[], secret_detected, injection_detected, base_score, known_tool, timestamp, _auth{authenticated,kya_level,client_id}, upgrade{...}}. For policy_preflight: {request_id, tool_name, agent_id, caller_identity{authenticated,kya_level,kya_score}, decision(allow|deny|require_approval), risk_score, matched_policies[], reason, rate_status{per_minute,per_hour,per_day}}. Other tools return their own JSON.
quirks: This is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server named 'AgentGuard' v2.0.0, not a plain REST endpoint — you must speak JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, tools/list, tools/call). serverInfo advertises protocolVersion 2025-03-26.
FREE and anonymous: every tested call returned HTTP 200 with a real result and no 402/SIWX challenge; responses carry _auth.kya_level='ANONYMOUS'. Cost $0.

PARTIAL SURFACE: tools/list advertises 25 tools but only 8 are callable anonymously. The other 17 (e.g. audit_log_write, secret_exposure_check, payload_safety_check, session_validate, emergency_kill, threat_intel_check, output_safety_scan) return {"error":"AUTH_REQUIRED", ... Register at https://feedoracle.io/mcp/register}. That gate is an upstream Bearer token (OAuth at feedoracle.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server), NOT x402 or SIWX — so those operations are intentionally excluded from this entry.
The 8 PUBLIC (free, no-auth) tools are: policy_preflight, tool_risk_score, approval_required, approval_list, decision_explain, policy_register, tool_manifest_verify, guard_metrics.

The governance engine is a self-hosted policy simulator (fixed tiers T1-T4, default spend/rate limits, canned policies like pol-001 'block payment tools without approval') — it evaluates the tool_name/tool_args you pass; it does not observe or intercept your real tool calls. Treat it as advisory, not enforcement.
Responses include a non-standard 'upgrade' block (v/type/next[]/mesh) nudging you toward follow-up tools — cosmetic, safe to ignore.
audit_log_query/audit_log_write are auth-gated, so approval_list/guard_metrics over anonymous access only ever reflect data written by authenticated tenants (typically empty for anonymous callers).
usage.guide: AgentGuard is a free MCP guardrail server for vetting AI-agent tool-calls. Connect over JSON-RPC 2.0 at POST https://tooloracle.io/guard/mcp/. Call flow: (1) send an 'initialize' request once, (2) optionally 'tools/list', (3) 'tools/call' with {name, arguments}; the result comes back stringified in result.content[0].text. Only 8 tools are free/anonymous — the rest need a feedoracle.io Bearer token and are not indexed. Free tools: policy_preflight (allow/deny/require_approval decision for a proposed tool_name+tool_args), tool_risk_score (0-100 risk score with factors/secret/injection flags), approval_required (does this call need human sign-off; register_pending to mint an approval_url), approval_list (list pending/approved/denied approvals), decision_explain (human-readable rationale for a decision), policy_register (browse the T1-T4 policy tiers/tools/rules), tool_manifest_verify (scan an MCP tool's description/publisher/domain for injection & supply-chain risk), guard_metrics (operational decision/risk stats). Example: tools/call name='tool_risk_score' arguments={tool_name:'transfer_funds', tool_args:{amount:5000000, recipient:'0xabc'}, agent_id:'my-agent'} -> risk_score 75, risk_level 'high', recommendation 'Require human approval'. Note the policy engine only scores the arguments you hand it; it does not intercept your live agent runtime.

entries.name: Agentstools PII Scan
entries.description: Detect structured PII in a text blob (emails, phone numbers, credit cards, IBAN, US SSN/ITIN/EIN/routing, Medicare ids, passports, driver licenses, IPv4/IPv6/MAC, Bitcoin/Ethereum addresses, dates of birth, geo coordinates and secrets/API keys) using deterministic regex + checksum validators, returning per-finding type and confidence plus a compliance summary — a detection-only pre-LLM/DLP guardrail (use /pii/redact to also get transformed text).

text.description: The text to scan for PII (required)

entities.description: Optional allow-list of entity types to scan for (default: all). See GET /pii/recognizers.

include_positions.description: Include character start/end offsets per finding (off by default for privacy)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/pii/scan with a JSON body: text (required — the text blob to scan). Optional: entities[] (allow-list of entity types to restrict to; default all — enumerate via free GET /pii/recognizers) and include_positions (bool — add character start/end offsets per finding, off by default for privacy). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: {object:'pii_scan', input_bytes, summary{total_findings, counts_by_type{<TYPE>:n}, compliance_categories{GDPR|PCI|HIPAA:n}, has_pii}, findings[]{type (e.g. EMAIL, CREDIT_CARD), score (0-1 confidence), compliance_tags[]}, findings_truncated, pack_version, disclaimer}. Detection only — no transformed/redacted text is returned.
quirks: text is the only required input; the object being scanned is the caller's own supplied text — nothing is crawled or fetched (no network side effect).
Detection ONLY — the response never echoes the matched PII value or transformed text; each finding is just {type, score, compliance_tags}. Use /pii/redact for the redacted/transformed text.
include_positions is off by default (for privacy); set include_positions:true to get character start/end offsets per finding.
Optional entities[] restricts the scan to specific entity types (enumerate the recognizer ids via the free GET /pii/recognizers).

STRUCTURED PII only (deterministic patterns + checksums: Luhn for cards, mod-97 for IBAN, ABA routing, SSN/ITIN structure). Free-text person/organization/location NAMES are OUT OF SCOPE — has_pii:false is not proof the text is PII-free.
Indicators, not legal advice and not a compliance guarantee — always review before relying on it.
Sibling /pii/redact on the same host is a separate service (returns transformed text), not an alias of this detection-only route.
usage.guide: Run this on any text BEFORE forwarding it to a third-party LLM/API to enforce GDPR/HIPAA/PCI handling. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/pii/scan with {text:'<blob to scan>'} (optionally entities:['EMAIL','CREDIT_CARD',...] to narrow, or include_positions:true for offsets). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base.
